subject: Discovery recap: Observability + Evals (dashboards, tracing, golden prompts, rollout guardrails)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Lee <jamie@zenhealth.ai>, Priya Singh <priya@zenhealth.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 06 May 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Observability + Evals (ZenHealth)

Thanks again for the conversation today — great to meet the ZenHealth team. Below is a short recap of what we heard, success criteria you mentioned, and proposed next steps. Please correct me where I missed anything.

Quick recap of pain points you shared
- Lack of end-to-end observability when models regress in production (slow detection, unclear root cause).
- No standardized "golden prompt" sets or automated regression alerts tied to deployment rollouts.
- Difficulty correlating user-facing failures with specific model checkpoints, prompt variants, or rollout events.
- Current evals are ad-hoc; need continuous, automated checks integrated into deploy pipeline.

Current stack
- Inference: AWS SageMaker real-time endpoints (in-house wrapper), some edge caching.
- Monitoring: Datadog for infra, but no model-level telemetry or prompt tracing.
- Evals: internal runner that runs nightly suites, not yet tied to canary rollouts.

Success criteria you described
1) Detect regressions within 10 minutes of rollout with clear signal to owners.
2) Dashboards showing per-prompt, per-model, and per-region latency + quality trends.
3) Golden prompt sets for critical intents to run pre/post-rollout regressions.
4) Alerting + playbooks for canary failures and automatic rollback guardrails.

What Redwood can deliver (high level)
- Token- and prompt-level tracing hooks plus per-request metadata that surfaces in dashboards.
- Out-of-the-box dashboards (per-route, per-model, golden-prompt delta charts) and regression alerts tied to configurable thresholds.
- Eval integration: schedule/trigger eval suites on version pins and canary cohorts, with diffs and triage UI.
- Rollout policies: canary + automatic rollback on detected metric regressions; manual approval gates if desired.

Attachments: I attached a short primer on Redwood observability and an example golden-prompt CSV for reference.

Proposed next steps
- Technical deep dive (60 min): connect your infra + datadog team to discuss tracing hooks and data flow. Owner: Marissa (me) to schedule.
- Provide golden-prompt candidates and an example baseline eval you want us to run against a canary. Owner: Jamie/Priya to share by EOD Tue.
- Access for a Redwood sandbox: Connor to provision test project + eval harness.

Would you be available for a technical deep dive next week? I can do Tuesday or Thursday mornings (PT).

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
Attach: redwood-observability-primer.pdf (PDF), golden-prompts-zenhealth.csv (CSV)

From: Jamie Lee <jamie@zenhealth.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@zenhealth.ai>, Sam Torres <sam.torres@zenhealth.ai>
Date: Thu, 07 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Observability + Evals (ZenHealth)

Thanks Marissa — this is great and captures the conversation well. A few clarifications and notes from our side:

Clarifications
- The 10-minute detection target is soft — priority is actionable alerts with low false positives; if we can get reliable detection in 15–20 min that's acceptable.
- Evals: our nightly runner currently has 1k prompts but needs segmentation by intent and confidence buckets. We can provide exports.

Stakeholders to loop in for the technical deep dive
- Sam Torres (infra lead) — network, VPC peering and IAM constraints.
- Priya Singh (ML engineering lead) — eval definitions, golden prompt selection, thresholding.

We'll aim to share an initial golden prompt set and a sample eval CSV by EOD Tuesday (May 12).

Tuesday morning PT works for us for the deep dive. Suggest 10:00 AM PT.

One ask: can Redwood show an example of the regression alerting workflow (how alerts map to rollbacks and playbooks) during the deep dive? That's a key decision factor for us.

—Jamie
